learning_outcomes.description: Apply disciplinary knowledge and skills within an authentic professional workplace relevant to the student's field of study.
Demonstrate professional conduct, communication and engagement with workplace practices, policies and expectations.
Develop and demonstrate career management, networking, and professional communication skills relevant to future employment.
Critically reflect on the placement experience to evaluate personal strengths, skill development, future learning needs and career opportunities.

assessments.task_description:
The Learning Contract is to be completed during the first week of placement. Students will define their placement goals, list learning objectives and the activities that will enable them to achieve these learning objectives.

The Risk Assessment is also to be completed during the first week of placement. Students will identify hazards associated with placement activities and discuss any required risk management/training with their supervisor.

Templates for the Learning Contract and Risk Assessment are available on the course Blackboard site under Assessment. Both the Learning Contract and Risk Assessment must be endorsed by the Placement Supervisor prior to submission.
assessments.submission_guidelines: You will submit your Assessment task in Blackboard via the submission link for the assessment by the submission deadline. You should also retain an electronic copy of every piece of assessment you submit.

assessments.task_description:
Students will work through a series of nine online training modules focussed on building and developing their employability and professional skills. The modules have been developed by the UQ Careers and Employability Team. The modules are grouped into three distinct blocks, which students are recommended to complete in a phased manner linked to their progress through their placement. After completing each block of three modules, students will complete an online quiz to assess their learning.

The modules are as follows:

1. Getting started with your placement and the workplace (complete in first 40 hours of placement):

  • Crash course into employer expectations
  • Developing your workplace toolkit
  • Understanding your professional self


2. Effective communication and making the most of your placement (complete between 40-80 hours of placement):

  • Developing strategies to have a conversation with industry
  • Getting started with networking
  • Developing a winning elevator pitch


3. Reflecting on your placement and preparing for your career (complete between 80-120 hours of placement):

  • Articulating your experience to prospective employers
  • Introduction to interviews
  • Identifying your career pathways


Students will calculate their own schedule for completing the modules and the associated quizzes. All quizzes must be completed by the end of placement.

Each quiz requires achievement of a minimum score of 7/10 to pass. Students have a maximum of two attempts to pass each quiz.

Students are responsible for ensuring a stable internet connection while undertaking an online quiz.

Troubleshooting – if students experience any technical difficulties during the online quiz:

  • Do not close the browser window.
  • Contact AskUs immediately: support.my.uq.edu.au/app/chat/chat_launch_lib – if the technical issue cannot be resolved, ask for a copy of the chat.
  • Document the problem – if you receive an error message or similar, take a copy of the message, note the time/date of the problem, which web browser you used, exactly what you were doing at the time and any other relevant information.
  • Email your course coordinator (copy in AGFS Admin – agriculture@enquire.uq.edu.au) with your documented evidence and a copy of the AskUs chat. Any delays in this communication being received may impact the advice that could be provided to you.

assessments.task_description:
Students will deliver a three-minute presentation using a single PowerPoint slide to share details of their placement and to reflect on their experience.

Each presentation should briefly introduce where you went on placement and then use the SEAL Reflection Method to communicate your experience. Training on using the SEAL Reflection Method will be provided in the pre-placement workshop.

The presentation should be designed for a general audience (i.e., not too technical) and convey details of activities undertaken during placement without breaching any confidentiality restrictions of the host organisation.

All students will deliver their presentation live via Zoom during one of the presentation seminars regardless of whether the placement hours have been partially or fully completed. Note: if your placement dates clash with this, you must seek 'time off' from your placement.

All students must attend the first 1-hour presentation seminar (this follows directly after the post-placement workshop) and be ready to present. A second presentation seminar is scheduled for later on the same day; this is an overflow and will be used only if needed, i.e., depending on student numbers. For identity verification, students must turn on their camera and hold up their student ID card. Students must show their face on screen the entire time to receive a grade.

assessments.task_description: Prior to completion of your placement, UQ will send a request to your placement supervisor to complete an assessment of your performance in the workplace and to endorse the hours you claimed to have worked; students must keep a diary of their hours and activities and provide this to their supervisor at completion of the placement. Supervisors will submit this report at the completion of your placement directly to UQ. Supervisors will be encouraged to use the report as an opportunity to provide formal feedback to you. The feedback will be released to students following review by UQ.

learning_activities.topic:
Placement

Students will undertake a minimum of 120 hours (recommended maximum 160 hours) placement in an approved workplace between these dates. Note: if placement dates clash with workshop dates, students must seek 'time off' from their placement to attend compulsory workshops.

Students must keep a diary of their hours and activities and provide this to their supervisor at completion of the placement.
